mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals strengthening labor market conditions, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 0.5% annually, it signals monetary tightening that compresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in FEDFUNDS combined with rising RSAFS indicates accommodative monetary policy supporting consumer credit demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS decline and RSAFS rise fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and INDPRO decline > 0.5% YoY), S&P 500 experiences negative returns over 60 days due to reduced growth and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate improving consumer confidence and economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 1.0% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 7.0%, it signals labor market tightening that increases wage pressures and corporate costs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 7.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signal robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and INDPRO fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion (INDPRO > 100 and HOUST decline > 0.5% MoM), S&P 500 experiences negative returns over 20 days due to overheating and policy tightening.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
